findings.quote: If a motor or a push from outside adds energy, the system is not isolated, and its total energy rises.
findings.problem: Incoming energy does not necessarily raise the system's total energy. Energy can leave at the same time. A motor can supply work while an equal amount leaves as heat, leaving stored energy unchanged. The change depends on net energy transfer.
findings.source: [OpenStax, College Physics 2e, §15.1: The First Law of Thermodynamics](https://openstax.org/books/college-physics-2e/pages/15-1-the-first-law-of-thermodynamics).

findings.quote: A real machine wastes some energy as heat and sound. So its efficiency is below $100\%$. Only an ideal machine with no waste reaches $100\%$.
findings.problem: This is false as a general rule for useful-energy efficiency. Heat can be the useful output. Real electric resistance heaters convert electrical input into useful heat at 100% efficiency at the point of use. The statement needs a restriction to machines whose useful output excludes that heat.
